description: A-1 stage 3 exterior geometry corrections for CAP 487, applied to the pinned donor mesh at load time by both the converter and the measurement harness. Every entry names the dimension it closes, the sourced target, and why this transform was chosen. Corrections are deliberately parametric and version-controlled here rather than baked into a mesh, because the donor mesh is GPL and stays outside this repository (docs/FLIGHTGEAR_C182_GPL_PLAN.md).

corrections.rationale: TCDS 3A13 gives the McCauley B3D36C431/80VSA-1 a certification band of 77.5-79.0 in; the donor measured 79.255 in, outside it. This is a certification bound, not a tolerance, so the value must move. A radial scale about the existing propeller axis was chosen over clipping the blade tips because it preserves topology, vertex count, UVs and the hub position exactly, and at 0.32 percent the difference between scaling and trimming is under a third of a millimetre at the tip. FastProp, the blur disc, is scaled with the blades so the spinning propeller still matches the static one. chrome_spinner is deliberately NOT scaled: the spinner diameter is not the propeller diameter.
corrections.preserves: Hub position and rotation axis are unchanged by construction, because the transform only scales the component perpendicular to that axis. No animation pivot moves, so converter.PROP_ROTATION needs no recomputation.
corrections.source: TCDS 3A13 p.33 Propeller Limits, 182S/182T item (2); POH p.1-3 front view annotates 79" MAX

corrections.blocked_on: Which endpoints the POH three-view's wheel-track dimension actually marks. Ron or an SME, not a model.
corrections.rationale: READING SETTLED 2026-09-15 as CENTRE-TO-CENTRE, by convergent inference rather than by reading POH Fig 1-1 Sheet 1 - nobody involved has the POH. The ambiguity flips the SIGN (centre-to-centre 102.99 in, -4.64%, too NARROW; tyre outer face 109.45 in, +1.34%, too WIDE), so the grounds matter. (1) THE POH'S OWN NOTE, on the companion gear dimension of the same three-view, measures wheel base 'nose wheel axle -> main wheel CENTRE LINE' (dimension master line 96, sourced POH Fig 1-1 Sheet 2 NOTE). A drawing that annotates one gear dimension to the wheel centreline is not measuring the other to the tyre faces. (2) CONSISTENCY, which is arithmetic rather than opinion: every other donor dimension is undersized - overall length -2.48%, overall height -2.78%, wheel base -3.64% - so the centre-to-centre reading makes the gear uniformly small like the rest of the airframe, while the outer-face reading makes the track the ONLY oversized dimension on the model and has it 1.34% too wide while its own wheelbase is 3.64% too short, which is not a plausible mesh. (3) Standard aeronautical convention measures landing gear track centre to centre; note that FAA-H-8083-31B uses 'tread' for the TYRE's rubber crown, which is the likely source of the original doubt. SOURCES CHECKED AND FOUND SILENT: EASA/FAA TCDS 3A13 gives the datum, levelling means and 6.00x6 main tyre size but no tread; Cessna's Specification and Description Skylane 182T Dec 2015 Rev C lists height, length, span, cabin and doors but no wheel track at all. THE TRANSFORM: each wheel moves outboard 0.0636 m (2.5 in), 1.3080 -> 1.3716 m half-track. A single spanwise scale would be wrong - scaling the wheel about an inboard root widens the TYRE too, taking the donor's 164 mm wheel to 193 mm - so MainWheel and WheelFairing TRANSLATE rigidly, keeping their own dimensions, and only MainStrut ramps, with its inboard attachment at |x|=0.938 m fixed and its outboard end taking the full delta. That is the spring leg flexing outward rather than growing. This is the MESH, not the ACF flight model's gear positions.
corrections.source: POH p.1-3, Figure 1-1 Sheet 1 (front view); ambiguity recorded in c182t_dimension_master.json
corrections.evidence_strength: INFERRED, not read off the drawing. Weaker than the propeller (a certification bound) or the horizontal tail span (a direct measurement), and recorded as such.

corrections.rationale: CORRECTED 2026-09-15, and the earlier blocking reason was wrong about the decomposition. It said the stabiliser lives inside Airframe with the wings, so a spanwise scale would shrink the WINGS. Airframe carries only the stabiliser TIP CAPS: at z 4.8-6.3 it has 738 vertices at |x| <= 0.2 (tailcone and fin) and 156 at |x| 1.600-1.816, with nothing in between. The surface itself is the Elevator object (427 vertices, |x| 0.510-1.821) plus ElevatorTrim. The wings sit at z 0.548-1.815, so a z-window of 4.8-6.3 provably selects zero wing vertices - checked, not assumed. Airframe is therefore region-selected and the two elevator objects are transformed whole, since they are entirely tail. The transform anchors at the root station |x| = 0.51 m, where the elevator meets the fuselage, so that junction is a fixed point and the skin cannot tear; everything outboard closes proportionally. The measured 1.8164 m half-span (143.03 in) goes to 1.778 m (140.0 in).
corrections.also_found: The master's ambiguity note for this target says the stabiliser and elevator tips 'are flush on this airframe'. In this donor they are not: the stabiliser half-span is 1.8164 m and the Elevator object reaches 1.8212 m, 0.189 in further per side. It does not change the verdict - both readings are about 3 in over the 140.0 in target - but the note should be corrected so the next reader does not treat the two as interchangeable. The same proportional transform is applied to the Elevator, so its 0.189 in per side overhang beyond the stabiliser is preserved rather than silently flushed - the donor's relationship is kept, not invented.
